objective: Add the final summary line to render_payslip's output in the exact format 'Summary: net=<net> gross=<gross> deductions=<total>' with 2-decimal values, and create tests/test_payslip_summary.py that asserts the exact line for employees e1 and e2.

concepts: render_payslip returns list[str]; the summary line is appended as the last element after the 'Net:' line
f-string 2-decimal formatting :.2f for net, gross, and the deductions total
total = sum of all deduction amounts; order-independent

inputs: frozen contract C2 spec (the exact summary-line format, stage-contract.json#shared_contracts C2)
frozen contract C1 spec (the pay shape the summary is computed from)
employee fixture records e1/e2 in payroll/employees.py
non_goals: Do not modify payroll/calc.py (owned by T01; the summary line must not change the calculation)
Do not touch payroll/legacy_export.py — no summary line in the XML (HR-4411 byte format)
Do not modify the existing tests in tests/test_payroll.py (owned by T01)
Do not change the existing payslip lines (header, blank line, Gross, deduction lines, Net) — only append the final summary line
Do not add any dependency, including a new test framework
implementation_constraints: The summary line is computed from the compute_pay result: pay['net'], pay['gross'], and the sum of all deduction amounts
Exact format: 'Summary: net=' + f"{net:.2f}" + ' gross=' + f"{gross:.2f}" + ' deductions=' + f"{total:.2f}" — no spaces around '=', no thousands separators
Append the line as the last element of the returned list; no trailing newline, no extra blank line
stdlib only; unittest style matching tests/test_payroll.py

deliverables.what: render_payslip ending with the exact 2-decimal summary line
exact-format summary tests for e1 and e2

acceptance_tests.description: render_payslip('e1') returns a list whose last element is exactly 'Summary: net=6000.00 gross=8000.00 deductions=2000.00' and the element before it is 'Net: 6000.00'
acceptance_tests.evidence: run test test_summary_line_exact_format via python -m unittest tests.test_payslip_summary; the test asserts lines[-1] equals the exact summary string and exits 0

acceptance_tests.description: render_payslip('e2') returns a list whose last element is exactly 'Summary: net=2700.00 gross=3600.00 deductions=900.00'
acceptance_tests.evidence: the same test test_summary_line_exact_format covers e1 and e2 in one run; python -m unittest tests.test_payslip_summary exits 0

acceptance_tests.description: A summary line written as 'Summary: net=6000 gross=8000 deductions=2000' (no 2 decimals) or missing entirely fails the exact-equality test
acceptance_tests.evidence: the exact-equality assertEqual fails with the observed-vs-expected diff when the formatting is wrong

acceptance_tests.description: render_payslip('e999') raises KeyError from employees.get_employee exactly as before; no summary line is rendered and no new exception type is introduced
acceptance_tests.evidence: the unit test asserts render_payslip('e999') raises KeyError (assertRaises) in tests/test_payslip_summary.py; python -m unittest exits 0

failure_cases.scenario: A future deduction set with more than two entries
failure_cases.expected_behavior: the summary line prints deductions=<total> where total is the sum of all entries; the line format is unchanged
The summary prints deductions=0.00 (sum over an empty list is 0); no crash

handoff.notes: The summary line is the last list element of render_payslip; T03 shape-checks the format against C2 and T04 verifies it end-to-end. Do not add the line to legacy_export.py.

warnings.detail: T01 and T02 share the small compute_pay contract and both run the pre-existing test suite
warnings.rationale: Kept split: owned paths are disjoint, frozen C1 unlocks true parallelism, and the shared model is a 3-key dict (not a complex state model); merging would serialize two independent changes without meaningful context saving
